I am a 38-year-old man in Quzhou. I finished middle school and came back to the village three years ago after working in a factory in Shijiazhuang. My father handed me the management of our 340 mu farm when his back got too bad for fieldwork. With my wife, my father, and my school-age son, we are four mouths to feed, so I cannot afford big mistakes.

Three hundred and forty mu is a lot of land for one household. I rely on machinery service teams for tillage, planting, and harvest—I own a small tractor, but most work is contracted out. I have a well for irrigation, which is my lifeline when the spring turns dry.

It is early March. My winter wheat is greening up. I planted improved Jimai-22 on about 280 mu last October, and it looks decent after the winter. I will topdress urea twice—once at green-up and again at jointing—totaling about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu. I will also put down compound fertilizer with phosphate and potash at roughly 6 kg P₂O₅ and 4 kg K₂O per mu. I will irrigate four times from my well: green-up, jointing, heading, and grain filling. That is what the high-yielding fields in my village do, and after only three years I still follow the experienced farmers. I will spray herbicide once and fungicide twice to control rust and scab. There is no tillage now—the crop is already in the ground.

Come early June, as soon as the wheat comes off, I will plant summer maize on those same 280 mu without ploughing—direct seeding right into the wheat stubble. Everyone here uses Denghai 605 hybrid seed; it is reliable and the grain dealer pays well for it. I will apply about 16 kg N, 5 kg P₂O₅, and 4 kg K₂O per mu, split between basal and jointing topdress. Three irrigations: seedling establishment, tasseling, and grain filling. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice for corn borer. I expect around 580 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

I keep 30 mu for spring soybean and 30.1 mu for oilseed—peanut, most likely, because the buyer from the county oil mill comes every autumn. I rotate these on the south plot that tends to stay a bit wetter. For soybean, I will rotary till in April, sow an improved Jidou variety, and apply only a little nitrogen—about 3 kg per mu—because the root nodules help, but I will give it 5 kg P₂O₅ and 3 kg K₂O. Two irrigations and two pesticide sprays. For the oilseed, I will deep plough to loosen the soil for pod development, then fertilize heavier: 10 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, 5 kg K₂O per mu. Three irrigations and three sprays. I expect 165 kg per mu from the soybean and 250 kg per mu from the oilseed.

I grow the soybean and oilseed partly for cash and partly to break pest cycles. With only three years of experience, I do not experiment much. I watch what my neighbors do, copy the ones who consistently get good yields, and keep my inputs balanced because fertilizer and diesel prices have been high.
